answer: Beacon-salted sequential admission: before each threshold-VRF beacon round, an agent commits a nonce plus a jade-tagged metadata hash and a walnut-sized challenge descriptor; the beacon then seeds a target on a ridge-shaped difficulty curve. The agent must return a fresh sequential proof within a short window. Since the seed is post-commitment and unpredictable, sybils cannot precompute or amortize solutions. Attacker cost scales linearly: one independent compute/storage/availability unit per identity per epoch, with that epoch’s routing slot forfeited on failure.
